Disease Outbreak Disrupts Turkish Media & Publishing Operations

A sudden outbreak of norovirus has impacted several major media and publishing firms in Istanbul and Ankara, industry sources reported on Thursday. The contagious virus, which causes severe gastrointestinal symptoms, has led to significant absenteeism among editorial staff, print workers, and distribution teams, causing widespread disruption across newsrooms and printing sites.

The Turkish Media & Publishing Association (TMPA) confirmed that at least 18 publishing houses and three national daily newspapers have reported infection clusters since Monday. “We are facing unprecedented challenges as up to 35% of onsite personnel are currently on sick leave,” said TMPA spokesperson Melis Yildiz. “Some print runs have been reduced, and delays in both publication and distribution are unavoidable.”

Several broadcasters have scaled back live programming, switching to pre-recorded content due to a shortage of technical and production staff. “We’re keeping essential news bulletins on air, but some talk shows and cultural segments have been postponed,” said a senior executive at Ada Media.

Analysts expect the outbreak’s effects to persist into next week, with financial losses mounting as advertising deadlines are missed and circulation figures drop. Ceyhun Güler, media sector analyst at Bosphorus Insights, noted, “If the situation continues, we may see lasting impacts on quarterly earnings and audience engagement metrics.”

TMPA is coordinating closely with health authorities and urging all industry employers to intensify workplace hygiene measures. The association has not announced any site closures but stated it is reviewing contingency plans as the situation develops.
